_readme: Every number this card runs on. The scripts read it; nothing is typed twice.
model_state.py carries a fallback copy of all of it, so a broken or missing
file cannot cost a card. When it falls back, the card says so.
WHAT IS MEASURED AND WHAT IS CHOSEN:
nothing here is measured. This card has no backtest yet, so every value under
'grading' is a decision somebody made, not a finding. The college card's
equivalent file separates the two and caps its grades by what its backtest
supports. Until 'backtest' below is filled in, the letters on this card are
claims no record stands behind, and that is worth knowing when reading them.
KNOWN GAP, ratings.seasons:
the fit sees 2025 only. That is right today, because the 2026 season has not
been played and last season regressed toward the mean is exactly what a prior
is. It stops being right the moment Week 1 is final: with no current season in
the list, a December card would still be rating teams on 2025 football. The
college model solves this with a half-life on the current season and a carry
weight on the prior one. Fixing it here is one edit to this list plus a carry
weight, and it is the next change due.
The staleness check in nfl_card.py cannot catch that. It compares the
modification time of power_ratings.csv, and the Tuesday rebuild rewrites that
file every week, so it stays permanently fresh while the data underneath is a
season old. A check that cannot fail is not a check.
